after.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{4})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ Given that the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
after.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =\frac{5\pi }{12}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{n\pi }{2}+\frac{5\pi }{24}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{24}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{17\pi }{24}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{29\pi }{24}$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{41\pi }{24}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{5\pi }{24},\frac{17\pi }{24},\frac{29\pi }{24},\frac{41\pi }{24}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{1}=\frac{5\pi }{24}$ and ${x}_{2}=\frac{17\pi }{24},$ we have

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{24}\cdot \frac{17\pi }{24}=\frac{85{\pi }^{2}}{576}.
$$

$$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{24}\cdot \frac{13\pi }{24}=\frac{13{\pi }^{2}}{576}.

after.problem: Consider the equation $\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-{45}^{∘})-\sqrt{3}=0$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-{45}^{∘})-\sqrt{3} & =0 \\ \sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-{45}^{∘}) & =\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-{45}^{∘}) & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-{45}^{∘}) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-{45}^{∘} & ={45}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ={45}^{∘}+{45}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ 2x & ={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ x & ={45}^{∘}+n\cdot {90}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={45}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={135}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x={225}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x={315}^{∘}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x={45}^{∘},{135}^{∘},{225}^{∘},{315}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ is $45\cdot 135=6\,075.$
